Here is the MyHeritage search URL to look for Josiah Barnes in the 1855 Massachusetts State Census:

---

**Open this search:**
[https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20822/1855-massachusetts-state-census?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Josiah+fnmo.1+ln.Barnes+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.birth+ey.1818&qevents=List](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20822/1855-massachusetts-state-census?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Josiah+fnmo.1+ln.Barnes+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.birth+ey.1818&qevents=List)

This search targets the 1855 Massachusetts State Census collection on MyHeritage and looks for Josiah Barnes. The results will show where he was living in 1855 and who was in his household. Look for a Josiah Barnes born around 1818 in Massachusetts, noting the town, household members, and their ages.

**Note:** MyHeritage ranks rather than filters results, so many hits are normal — the birth year moves closer matches toward the top. Log in first if prompted.

Once you have the page open, save it as a PDF (Cmd+P on Mac / Ctrl+P on Windows → Save as PDF) and upload it here, and the agent will triage the results for you.

> **Alternative:** FamilySearch also holds this census as "Massachusetts, State Census, 1855" and can be searched there as well.

- Log: log_001 (in-flight). Plan item pli_001 is now in_progress.
- The researcher needs to open the link, capture the results page and upload it. Triage comes back to search-external-sites after that.
- No conflicts are recorded, so I encoded name and birth year 1818.

---

Open this search:
https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20822/1855-massachusetts-state-census?s=1&formId=master&formMode=1&useTranslation=1&exactSearch=&p=1&action=query&view_mode=card&qname=Name+fn.Josiah+fnmo.1+ln.Barnes+lnmsrs.false&qevents-event1=Event+et.birth+ey.1818&qevents=List

It should show where Josiah Barnes was living in 1855 and who was in his household, with their ages and birthplaces. Look for a Josiah Barnes born about 1818 in Massachusetts, which means an age of about 37 in 1855. After the page loads, scroll to the bottom and back to the top, press Cmd+P (Mac) or Ctrl+P (Windows), choose Save as PDF, and upload it at https://genealogy.example.org/#/p/proj_7d4b2e91c6a05f38/upload. Log in to MyHeritage first if the page asks.

Two notes from the site. It ranks results rather than filtering them, so a large hit count is normal. The birthplace couldn't go into the link because the site takes only one event, so the birth year is used and you can check the place by eye. FamilySearch also holds "Massachusetts, State Census, 1855", so I can search that copy instead if you prefer.

Once you upload the capture, I'll go through the results and rate each match against Josiah.

Barnes" in Springfield, is only a possible match because it gives an initial and no household. The other two don't fit on age, birthplace or spelling. FamilySearch holds this same census collection too, so it can be searched there as well.

Next, please open the Concord Josiah Barnes record and save its page as a PDF so it can be examined and the original image traced.

output.text_response:
Here is what the search-external-sites agent found:

---

**Matricula – How to search for Wilhelm Kuhlmann's 1836 marriage in Ochtrup**

Matricula Online is a free archive of scanned Catholic church books. It has **no name search** — you must browse to the register manually:

1. Go to [https://data.matricula-online.eu/en/](https://data.matricula-online.eu/en/) and open **Suchen → Ortssuche**.
2. Type **Ochtrup** as the Ort (place). Ochtrup was in Westphalia, so look for the **Diocese of Münster**.
3. Open the parish entry and choose the **Trauungen (marriages)** volume covering **1836**.
4. Page through to find Wilhelm Kuhlmann's entry. Note spelling variants: **Wilhelm / Guilielmus**, **Kuhlmann / Kulmann / Köhlmann**.

The marriage entry should give the date, the bride's name, and possibly both fathers' names.

**Note:** Matricula may not hold every parish; if Ochtrup is absent, the register exists on FamilySearch film instead (see below).

---

**FamilySearch alternative**

FamilySearch holds the Ochtrup Catholic church book *"Kirchenbuch, 1667–1875"* (film **876540**), covering baptisms, marriages, and deaths for **1804–1865** — which includes 1836. This film is **not available online**; it can only be viewed at a **FamilySearch Center or affiliate library**.

FamilySearch also has indexed collections — **Germany, Marriages, 1558–1929** and **Germany, Prussia, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records, 1580–1974** — that could be searched by name. The search-records agent can run those searches.

---

**Next step:** Browse Matricula to the 1836 marriage register, save the page as a PDF (Ctrl+P / Cmd+P → Save as PDF), and upload it here for transcription and triage.
